name: mosaic_dfba_coculture
description: Process-bigraph COMPOSITION: two dynamic-FBA organisms (E. coli core + Lactobacillus iNF517) sharing one substrate pool and competing for glucose. Each model runs standalone in its own study; here they are coupled through a shared `substrates` store (FBA writes consumption deltas, so competition composes additively — no custom coupling process).

uptake_ecoli.doc:
Michaelis-Menten (Monod) substrate uptake — a saturating per-resource uptake rate Vₐ = Vmaxₐ·Sₐ/(Kmₐ + Sₐ) that rises linearly at low substrate and plateaus at Vmaxₐ once Sₐ ≫ Kmₐ.
   Vₐ = Vmaxₐ · Sₐ / (Kmₐ + Sₐ)   (mmol / gDW / hr, ≥ 0); concentrations are floored at zero so the rate is 0 at Sₐ = 0.

_contract.summary: Per-resource Michaelis-Menten uptake rate Vₐ = Vmaxₐ·Sₐ/(Kmₐ+Sₐ), saturating in substrate, emitted with the scheduling interval to drive a downstream FBA step.

inputs.substrates: Current environmental concentrations per resource (`map[concentration]`); negative/missing values read as 0.
inputs.biomass: Current biomass (`mass`); read for composite wiring, not used in the rate law.

outputs.uptakes: Per-resource uptake rates Vₐ (`overwrite[map[float]]`), one entry per configured resource, ≥ 0.
outputs.interval: The scheduling interval Δt (`overwrite[float]`), echoed so the non-temporal FBA step can convert fluxes to deltas.

config.resources: List of resource names the Process emits uptakes for.
config.kinetic_params: {resource: [Km, Vmax]} — half-saturation constant and maximum velocity per resource; every resource must be present or initialize() raises.

symbols.V\u2090: uptake rate of resource a (mmol / gDW / hr, ≥ 0) — the emitted `uptakes[a]`
symbols.S\u2090: concentration of resource a in the environment (floored at 0)
symbols.Vmax\u2090: maximum uptake velocity of resource a (mmol / gDW / hr)
symbols.Km\u2090: half-saturation constant of resource a: Sₐ at which Vₐ = Vmaxₐ/2
symbols.\u03b5: numerical epsilon (1e-12) keeping the rate finite and exactly 0 at Sₐ = 0
symbols.\u0394t: scheduling interval of the Process, echoed as `interval`

assumptions: Uptake follows single-substrate Michaelis-Menten / Monod kinetics, independent per resource (no competitive coupling).
Substrate concentrations are floored at zero; the rate is non-negative and 0 at Sₐ = 0.
Km and Vmax are constant over the simulation (no enzyme regulation or adaptation).

fba_ecoli.doc:
Steady-state flux-balance analysis (FBA) LP: maximize the biomass objective cᵀv subject to the mass-balance constraint S·v = 0 and flux bounds lb ≤ v ≤ ub, with exchange lower bounds driven by the incoming uptake rates (lb = -u). The optimal growth rate μ and exchange fluxes are integrated over the interval Δt into biomass and substrate deltas.
   max cᵀv  s.t.  S·v = 0,  lb ≤ v ≤ ub,  lb_exch,a = -uₐ
   Δbiomass = μ·biomass·Δt;   Δsubstrateₐ = vₐ·biomass·Δt (clamped ≥ -pool).

_contract.summary: Steady-state FBA linear program (max cᵀv s.t. S·v = 0, lb ≤ v ≤ ub) with uptake-driven exchange bounds, returning biomass and substrate deltas over the step interval.

inputs.uptakes: Per-resource uptake rates uₐ (`map[float]`, ≥ 0); set exchange lower bounds. Also the Step's trigger.
inputs.substrates: Current substrate pools (`map[concentration]`); used to clamp each delta so no pool goes negative.
inputs.biomass: Current biomass (`mass`); scales fluxes and growth into absolute deltas.
inputs.interval: Timestep Δt (`float`) emitted by the upstream temporal Process; deltas are zero when Δt ≤ 0.

outputs.substrates: Per-resource substrate deltas Δsubstrateₐ (`map[count]`), clamped to not exceed the available pool.

config.model_file: SBML filename / absolute path / cobrapy model name (e.g. "textbook") for the genome-scale model.
config.substrate_update_reactions: {resource_name: exchange_reaction_id} mapping each tracked resource to its exchange reaction.
config.bounds: {reaction_id: {lower, upper}} static flux-bound overrides applied at load (e.g. O2, ATPM).
config.biomass_reaction: Objective reaction id; defaults to the model's own objective when omitted.

symbols.v: vector of reaction fluxes (mmol / gDW / hr); the LP decision variables
symbols.S: stoichiometric matrix Sᵢⱼ (metabolite i × reaction j)
symbols.c: objective coefficient vector selecting the biomass reaction
symbols.c\u1d40v: objective value = growth rate μ of the biomass reaction
symbols.lb: per-reaction lower flux bounds (uptake direction for exchanges)
symbols.ub: per-reaction upper flux bounds (secretion direction for exchanges)
symbols.u\u2090: incoming uptake rate of resource a (≥ 0); sets exchange lb_exch,a = -uₐ
symbols.v\u2090: optimal exchange flux of resource a at the solution (signed)
symbols.\u0394t: interval over which fluxes are integrated (the input `interval`)
symbols.\u0394substrate\u2090: substrate change = vₐ·biomass·Δt, clamped so the pool stays ≥ 0

assumptions: Metabolism is at quasi-steady state within each step: S·v = 0 (no net internal metabolite accumulation).
The LP maximizes a single linear biomass objective; a non-optimal solver status yields zero deltas.
Uptake rates set only exchange lower bounds (lb = -u); substrate deltas are clamped so pools never go negative.
Fluxes and growth are constant over the interval Δt (explicit forward-Euler integration of dynamic FBA).
